reasoning: Set A takes the project all the way to building. It has a seven-milestone roadmap with Outline, Exit and Depends cells. M1 is a walking skeleton across eqdata, server and web. Its plan opens with one interface task, then step spines and thicken tasks, then wiring and a system task, and it has a full dependency graph with stated reasons. The todo list and 35 context packets are ready to use. The packets I sampled (T01, T05, T11) include the step tables, the frozen types and the golden cases a builder needs. A's quant design is strong: unadjusted prices are adjusted at query time, so later events don't leak into earlier dates; the PCA runs on each 252-day window; and every claim gets a paired or permutation test with Holm correction and is routed through the null-hypothesis-testing skill. Set B's design is also sound: per-window PCA, Marchenko–Pastur denoising, Ledoit–Wolf, purged splits, a harness with locked registrations, and the decision step run with null-hypothesis-testing. But B stops at design. Its roadmap lists stages only, with no milestones, no tasks/plan.md or todo.md, no CONSTRAINTS.md or AGENTS.md, and no context packets. So milestone quality, interface quality, dependency graph, task buildability and finding the next build step essentially fail for B. Its references can't sit on any milestone or in any task's Read list, and it has stale cross-references (research pipelines cite 'PL-14's open_loader', but PL-14 is a server pipeline). A's weaknesses are smaller: heavy ID density, replan and process notes kept in the plan, references.md naming stages instead of milestones, and a primary-source probe that failed and was run against localhost.

strengths: M1 is a full walking skeleton across three packages: Phase 0 interface, then parallel spines, then wiring, then a system task
Look-ahead handled well: prices stored unadjusted and adjusted at query time (AD-07), a per-window spectrum, and bitemporal known_on reads
Every feature, forecast and agent claim gets a defined null and Holm correction, routed through null-hypothesis-testing; data-analysis is used in study, features and EDA
Context packets include the step tables, frozen types, golden cases and Writes lists
Point-in-time S&P 500 universe, matching the user's stated preference
weaknesses: Very dense IDs and long Deferred lists are hard reading for a solo learner
Replan notes and process narration are kept in plan.md
references.md lists stages ('S2, S3') where it should list milestones (the roadmap uses M4/M5)
The primary-source probe PB-01 failed and was run against localhost, so the real Sharadar path is still unvalidated

strengths: Clear five-package architecture with import rules enforced by import-linter
A testing harness with locked registrations, guarded views and per-candidate verdicts (AD-19)

No interface task and no dependency graph
A dollar-volume universe of about 1,000 stocks is the main path; the user's preferred point-in-time S&P 500 is only a fallback
